## D-36 staleness caveat

**This run predates the local matrix work and therefore describes the OLDER `ci.yml` on
`origin/main` (`67998e0b`), not the current local pipeline.** The matrix commits
`cce7f409` and `8fe32c6b` were never pushed to `origin`, so nothing in the capture below
reflects the `lane: [min, current]` matrix, the aggregate `CI required` gate, or any
timeout/cost surgery planned in this phase. A future reader must not mistake these
failures for the state of the pipeline after Phase 198 lands.

Corroborating evidence inside the capture: the job is named `Run test suite` with no
matrix suffix (`Run test suite (min)` / `Run test suite (current)` never appear), which
is only possible on the pre-matrix `ci.yml`.

## Failure summary (derived from the capture below; the capture itself is authoritative)

**`Compile without optional deps`** — 369 log lines. Compilation error, not a test failure:

```
error: module Phoenix.Controller is not loaded and could not be found.
error: module Phoenix.Component is not loaded and could not be found.
== Compilation error in file lib/threadline/operator_surface/ui.ex ==
** (CompileError) lib/threadline/operator_surface/ui.ex: cannot compile module Threadline.OperatorSurface.UI (errors have been logged)
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**`Run test suite`** — 673 log lines. `1124 tests, 3 failures, 1 excluded`, exit code 2:

1. `test/threadline/operator_surface/formless_pages_test.exs:56` — "display-only
   operator-surface pages stay formless / coverage_live.ex contains no
   `<input>`/`<select>`/`<textarea>`/`<form>`" (`Threadline.OperatorSurface.FormlessPagesTest`)
2. `test/threadline/v1_23_charter_doc_contract_test.exs:15` — "PROJECT.md locks active
   milestone posture and latest shipped framing" (`Threadline.V123CharterDocContractTest`)
3. `test/threadline/operator_surface/stress_router_test.exs:267` — "example app mounts
   audit and stress routes with a distinct live session"
   (`Threadline.OperatorSurface.StressRouterTest`)

The log also carries `** (Mix) Can't continue due to errors on dependencies`.

**`Example app browser E2E (Playwright)`** — 7814 log lines, the overwhelming majority of
the capture, and the run's wall-clock cost (≈1h 33m). Failures are all in the `[chromium]`
project and are a mix of `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed` / `element(s) not found`
and `locator.click: Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded`, e.g.:

- `tests/operator-earned-flows.spec.ts:145:7` — EF3 filtered timeline
- `tests/operator-features.spec.ts:184:7` — copy button
- `tests/operator-find-mobile.spec.ts:62:7` — transaction mobile
- `tests/operator-find-mobile.spec.ts:80:7` — row-history mobile

and PEM private-key headers. **No matches.** GitHub's own masking is visible in the log as

Run test suite	UNKNOWN STEP	2026-06-26T02:55:40.8126679Z          "# Threadline\n\n## What This Is\n\nThreadline is an open-source audit platform for Elixir teams using Phoenix, Ecto, and PostgreSQL. It combines trigger-backed row-change capture, first-class application action semantics (actor, intent, request/job context), and operator-grade exploration tools. It is built for teams who need audit trails that are hard to bypass, SQL-queryable without blobs, and genuinely useful for support and ops — not just compliance.\n\n## Core Value\n\nEvery row mutation that matters is captured durably and linked to who did it and why — without the developer having to remember to opt in.\n\n## Current State\n\nThreadline is in milestone **v1.38 Operator UI Page-by-Page IA & Design-System Polish**, opened on 2026-06-26. The mounted `/audit` operator surface already has the v1.37 private component system, stress route, ledger, theme coverage, accessibility/motion guardrails, and copy normalization; v1.38 now uses that substrate for a page-by-page cleanup focused on information architecture, task-led interaction groups, navigation clarity, responsive polish, and regression guardrails.\n\nThe highest-impact pass starts with the shell/home/timeline path so operators always know where they are and what to do next. Coverage follows as the audit-readiness workflow, then detail/governance/export surfaces, with accessibility, motion, docs, and adversarial closeout locking the result. PhoenixStorybook is scoped to the Phoenix example/dev lane; `/audit/__stress` remains the canonical runtime stress harness for operator flows. Core capture/query/auth semantics remain out of scope.\n\n## Current Milestone: v1.38 Operator UI Page-by-Page IA & Design-System Polish\n\n**Goal:** Make the operator UI feel deliberate, navigable, and task-led page by page while preserving v1.37's internal design-system substrate and the host-app-friendly library boundary.\n\n**Target features:**\n- **Baseline audit and guard repair** — current screenshots, route/selector inventory, stale planning cleanup, and any broken guardrail repair before page edits.\n- **PhoenixStorybook example/dev lane** — component/state stories for the existing private operator components without making PhoenixStorybook a root `threadline` dependency or public component API.\n- **Shell, home, and Timeline cleanup** — clear nav, page titles, active states, orientation affordances, primary tasks, filters, result states, and responsive behavior.\n- **Coverage audit-readiness flow** — schema scope, readiness hierarchy, duplicate remediation, and contextual transitions into Timeline without page-level distraction.\n- **Detail, governance, and export surfaces** — transaction, actor, row history, redaction, retention, evidence, and export pages reviewed as coherent operator workflows.\n- **A11y, motion, docs, and closeout** — keyboard/focus/reduced-motion checks, visual QA matrix, docs alignment, and an adversarial review that prevents regressions.\n\n## Latest Milestone Shipped: v1.37 Operator Surface Design-System Stress Test & Component System (2026-06-20)\n\n**Goal (achieved):** Turn the frozen-token / class-soup `/audit` operator surface into a systematically audited, internally-componentized design system, verified fractally from foundations through primitives, groups, pages, flows, copy, accessibility, motion, and final adversarial closeout.\n\n**Shipped:**\n- **Stress-lab harness and ledger** - `/audit/__stress`, static ugly-data fixtures, scored ledger, `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` projection, and screenshot ratchet guards.\n- **Internal design system** - private primitives, overlays, form controls, data-display helpers, layout/meta-components, and group stories with contract tests and no public component API.\n- **Operator shell and data surfaces** - consistent navigation, page headers, breadcrumbs, pager, theme picker, copyable full-value refs, data states, coverage flattening, destructive action confirmation, and page stress coverage.\n- **Copy, accessibility, and motion closeout** - brand/domain copy sweep, WCAG/APG source and browser guards, reduced-motion proof, automated accessibility-tree evide" <> ...
